title: Counterpart Fairness – Addressing Systematic Between-group Differences in Fairness Evaluation
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. It proposes a fairness index called Counterpart Fairness (CFair) to evaluate algorithmic fairness by accounting for systematic differences and confounding effects between groups defined by protected variables like race and gender.
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its key finding is that standard group-based fairness metrics can be misleading when systematic differences exist between groups, and the proposed Counterpart Fairness (CFair) index can reveal significant biases that are otherwise overlooked, as demonstrated on the MIMIC and COMPAS datasets.
